items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: He loved my last name originally, Gubenko, so he called me Gubenko.

ctx.x: Excellent. When I got to about the middle of the book and I turned the page and I saw the title of the chapter Foggo, I said I know who he’s going to talk about now.

You know everybody has a Benny Goodman story but not everybody living — one of my most fun times is I used to do a lot of the jazz cruises, you know, 90 musicians would be on a cruise. And Mel Powell was on one of the cruises. And Mel Powell worked with Benny Goodman way before I did. And we sat there one night talking about Benny Goodman stories, and who else? Maybe Ken Peplowski, he worked for Benny Goodman. Whoever was there that knew Benny Goodman, and it was actually like a bunch of comedians sitting around…

of them, the agent, he told Joe Glaser, “Get me” this is in New York, “Get me Ziggy Elman.” Ziggy Elman was in California. So I go to the first rehearsal I went with Joe Glaser to Benny’s rehearsal, even though I wasn’t going to be on the show I just wanted to hear the band. And I’m standing with Joe Glaser and Benny looks at me and he says, “I asked you to get me Ziggy Elman on the trumpet” he says. “That’s Ziggy Elman, I flew him in” and Joe Glaser would use every F word in the world, you know I’m telling you,…
